thesis: Mishra’s Factory solved a control deck’s oldest tension by being both a land and a threat, then added combat depth through the ability of Assembly-Workers to reinforce one another.

canonicalIdentity.currentOracleText: {T}: Add {C}. {1}: This land becomes a 2/2 Assembly-Worker artifact creature until end of turn. It's still a land. {T}: Target Assembly-Worker creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.
canonicalIdentity.identityNotes: IDs, first-printing date, and artist retained from the accepted card-data snapshot. Current abilities and control-duration ruling checked against the official MH2 FAQ. Removed the inherited field that mislabeled modern Oracle wording as original printed text.

originalContext.setEnvironment: Antiquities, 1994: the accepted printing snapshot identifies four seasonal illustrations of one land.
originalContext.designPurpose: Rules-based analysis: one land can supply mana, become an artifact creature, or pump an Assembly-Worker. No claim about undocumented original designer intent.
originalContext.initialReception: No new contemporary reception claim is made. The revised history uses dated registrations and a later, attributed design retrospective.

loreContext.summary: Seasonal industrial setting shown by the retained original illustrations; no invented canonical story event.

competitiveTimeline.event: Card and Board Old School tournament
competitiveTimeline.significance: Organizer results and deck photographs document Factory inside a black-white creature and removal deck. The vignette is a reconstruction, not match coverage.
Primary submitted registration contains four Mishra’s Factory, three Standstill, and two Faerie Conclave. No placement is claimed.
Rosewater explains why Foundry restricts its pump to attacking Assembly-Workers, identifying Factory’s defensive 3/3 as a design concern.

playbook.role: A mana source that becomes a threat when combat justifies the payment and exposure.
playbook.deckRequirements: Provide enough colored sources for ordinary spells and separate mana for animation if Factory must attack or block.
playbook.copyCount: Galli’s submitted list has four; this observation is not a universal recommendation.
playbook.mulligans: Count colored requirements: two Factories cannot cast Counterspell, and their own mana cannot both animate them and leave them untapped.
playbook.sequencing: Under modern rules, animate an older Factory with a different source, declare the block, then tap it to pump itself to 3/3. Leave it unanimated while resolving Nevinyrral’s Disk.
playbook.sideboarding: The value of an additional creature land depends on mana requirements and whether combat matters; no invented historical sideboard plan is asserted.
playbook.commonMistakes: A new animated Factory has summoning sickness for tap abilities; a new unanimated land may tap. Self-paying animation leaves it tapped. A self-pump to 3/3 does not survive Lightning Bolt.

counterplay.directAnswers: Swords to Plowshares and Lightning Bolt can remove an animated copy; Wasteland or Strip Mine can target the land without animation.
counterplay.engineDisruption: Attack colored mana and force the pilot to spend resources on defense instead of holding interaction.
counterplay.timingWindows: Wait for animation to resolve before creature or artifact removal. Factory remains a land while animated.
counterplay.racing: Larger creatures and trample can make an animation an expensive temporary defense rather than a profitable trade.
counterplay.sideboarding: Choose answer types for the actual permanent types and timing window, rather than treating an unanimated land as an artifact.

claims.summary: Control of the permanent since the start of the most recent turn, rather than time as a creature, determines attack and tap-symbol restrictions.
An older Factory can block and then tap to pump itself to 3/3; a tapped blocker deals damage under modern rules.
Animation adds artifact and creature types while retaining land. An unanimated Factory survives Disk; an animated one does not.
Galli’s February 21, 2026 registration has four Factories, three Standstills, and two Faerie Conclaves.
Raichlin won the twelve-player October 11, 2015 Card and Board event with the published black-white deck.
Rosewater attributes Foundry’s attacking-only pump to a deliberate move away from Factory’s strong defensive 3/3.
Both lands animate for one generic mana into a 2/2. Mutavault’s all-creature-types effect includes Assembly-Worker but does not add artifact type or Factory’s abilities.
Modern Horizons 2 notes explicitly permit animating an older Factory, blocking, and then tapping it to become 3/3; a newly controlled animated Factory cannot attack or use its tap abilities.
Rosewater explains that Foundry’s attacking-only pump restrains the defensive 3/3 available to Factory.
Galli’s February 21, 2026 Premodern sheet has four Factories, three Standstills and two Faerie Conclaves; no placement is claimed.
